title: Wikipedia: Another Brick in the Wall
content: Another Brick in the Wall is a three-part Pink Floyd composition from The Wall, released in 1979. Roger Waters wrote the song. Part 2 is associated with a children's choir, protest themes about oppressive schooling, and a disco-influenced production approach. The single topped the US Billboard Hot 100 and UK singles chart. Source summary prepared from Wikipedia, retrieved 2026-09-04. Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Wikipedia: Stars on 45 Medley
content: Stars on 45 was a Dutch pop act directed by producer Jaap Eggermont and known for medleys that recreated familiar songs over a common tempo and drum track. The Stars on 45 Medley was released in the early 1980s, reached number one in the United States, and was followed by the Long Play Album. Source summary prepared from Wikipedia, retrieved 2026-09-04. Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Wikipedia: Everybody Wants to Rule the World
content: Everybody Wants to Rule the World is a Tears for Fears song from Songs from the Big Chair, released in 1985. It was written by Roland Orzabal, Ian Stanley, and Chris Hughes and produced by Hughes. The new wave and synth-pop song addresses the desire for power and the effects of warfare. It reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100. Source summary prepared from Wikipedia, retrieved 2026-09-04. Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Wikipedia: Walk of Life
content: Walk of Life is a Dire Straits song from Brothers in Arms, released as a single in the United States in 1985 and the United Kingdom in 1986. Mark Knopfler wrote the song. Its arrangement combines rock and roll with a synthesizer-led keyboard riff and blues and zydeco influences. It reached number seven in the United States and number two in the United Kingdom. Source summary prepared from Wikipedia, retrieved 2026-09-04. Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Wikipedia: On and On and On
content: On and On and On is an ABBA song from Super Trouper, released as a single on 10 November 1980. It was written and produced by Benny Andersson and Bjorn Ulvaeus, with Agnetha Faltskog and Anni-Frid Lyngstad sharing lead vocals. Wikipedia describes the song as disco-rock and notes that it reached number 90 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and topped the US Dance Club Songs chart. Source summary prepared from Wikipedia, retrieved 2026-09-07. Wikipedia text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.
